before:
name: keyframer_worked_example
description: >
  Loadable demo of afield.stdlib/keyframer.kt — snapshotting, blending and persisting the live state
  of a sketch. Four pure-compute boxes, no Window and no Renderer: a KeyframeScope needs neither,
  because a uniform `Structure` is constructible bare and its bindings are plain maps, so the whole
  capture -> edit -> apply loop runs on the CPU. Each box draws its own result into its own output,
  via showPlaneGrid (drawToSVG -> display, so no AWT and no GPU) or plain display() HTML:
    1. keyframe_targets  — what a scope actually watches. Two uniform Structures registered as
                    targets, capture() into a Key, the Key edited and invoked to write it back, then
                    the live structures read back to prove the write landed. Shows the '@' rule:
                    everything after the last '@' is the property driven on the target, so
                    "glow@radius" and "blur@radius" both drive a plain `radius` on different
                    structures — and `glow@radius` itself is never bound on the structure. Also
                    shows that capture() reads binding-first-then-value, so a property written by
                    value snapshots too; it used to read bindings alone and return a silent null.
    2. keyframe_camera   — why a camera move is a screw motion. Two cameras a quarter turn apart,
                    both looking at the origin; sclerp (a rigid-transform interpolation, via
                    DualQuaternionf) against a naive lerp of the two positions. The sclerp path is a
                    circle: distance to the subject is constant at 8.2462 for the whole move and the
                    aim never leaves the origin by more than three millionths of a unit. Lerping the
                    positions cuts the corner and swings 27.2% closer at the midpoint, which reads on
                    screen as the subject lunging at the viewer. Both panels are FLines.
    3. keyframe_persist  — saving is always additive history. Three saveKey calls to a temp file,
                    each of which also appends a numbered copy to <file>.versions with a manifest;
                    keyVersions lists them. Shows what the KValue union does NOT carry (a Boolean, a
                    list and a null are dropped in silence, with no exception and no log line), and
                    how missingKey lets a scope that has grown a parameter still load an older file —
                    including the schema-qualified form that applies only to a matching
                    KeyDTO.schemaVersion. Prints version 0's JSON so the wire format is visible.
    4. keyframe_updatecode — the loop closing. Key.updateCode() emits the snapshot as pasteable
                    Kotlin, choosing literals so the paste round-trips as the same *type*: 0.65f
                    keeps its 'f' (without it a captured Float returns as a Double), 99L keeps its
                    'L', vectors become vec(...), StackSL stays stackSLString(...) rather than
                    decaying to a string, and an unsupported value becomes null behind an
                    /* unsupported */ comment so the code still compiles. The source block in this
                    box deliberately contains a '$': it must come out escaped, because a Kotlin raw
                    string would have interpolated it — a real defect found while writing
                    public/docs/keyframer_examples.md and fixed in the same branch.
  Replay this file into a fresh Field with the agent backdoor (field_run_transcript) to see all four
  on screen, then change a uniform, move a camera endpoint, add a value the union cannot carry, or
  edit the source block and re-run a box to watch the answer change. Each `execute` op omits inline
  code, so it runs the box's stored `code` property. Companion page:
  public/docs/keyframer_examples.md. Companion tests: afield.animation.keyframes.KeyframerTest.
operations:
  - create:
      box: keyframe_targets
      name: What a scope watches — capture, edit, apply
      frame: { x: 80.0, y: 80.0, w: 400.0, h: 100.0 }
      properties:
        code: |
          /*
          A KeyframeScope holds no values of its own. It holds *targets*: places to read from and
          write to. The simplest is a uniform Structure — and none of this needs a GPU, because
          Structure is constructible bare and bind/bindings are plain maps.
          */
          import afield.graphics.vulkan.buffers.Structure
          import afield.animation.keyframes.KeyframeScope
          
          val glow = Structure()
          val blur = Structure()
          glow.bind("radius") { 4.0f }
          glow.bind("intensity") { 0.35f }
          blur.bind("radius") { 12.0f }
          
          val scope = KeyframeScope()
          // The part after the last '@' is the property driven on the structure. Both passes have a
          // `radius`; the qualifier is the only thing keeping them apart inside the key.
          scope.target("glow@radius", glow)
          scope.target("glow@intensity", glow)
          scope.target("blur@radius", blur)
          
          // A snapshot. Reading only — capture() writes nothing anywhere.
          val captured = scope.capture()
          println("captured: " + captured.values.toSortedMap())
          
          // Fiddle, as you would with the sketch running, then make it so.
          val edited = captured.copy().update {
              this["glow@radius"] = 9.0f
              this["glow@intensity"] = 0.80f
          }
          edited()
          println(captured.diffText(edited, "captured", "edited"))
          
          // Read the live structures back. Note the write landed on the BARE property name.
          println("glow.radius    = " + glow.bindings["radius"]?.invoke())
          println("glow.intensity = " + glow.bindings["intensity"]?.invoke())
          println("blur.radius    = " + blur.bindings["radius"]?.invoke())
          println("glow.'glow@radius' = " + glow.bindings["glow@radius"]?.invoke() + "  <- never bound")
          
          // capture() reads a binding first and falls back to a plain value, so a property set with
          // `structure[name] = ...` (no bind) still lands in the key.
          val sneaky = Structure()
          sneaky.bind("bound") { 1.0f }
          sneaky["set"] = 2.0f
          val trapScope = KeyframeScope()
          trapScope.target("bound", sneaky)
          trapScope.target("set", sneaky)
          val trap = trapScope.capture()
          println("bound -> " + trap["bound"] + " ; set -> " + trap["set"] + " (present: " + ("set" in trap) + ")")
          
          // Put the original back and re-capture: a Key is a complete description of the scope.
          captured()
          val restored = scope.capture()
          
          /*
          markdown() rather than a hand-built card: headings for the captions, GFM tables for the
          key/value pairs, a fence for the multi-line diff. `key.h` and diffHtml() are HTML from
          other Field APIs and are *meant* to pass through, so they interpolate directly; every
          computed value carries `.md`, which a table cell effectively requires.
          */
          fun bound(s: Structure, k: String) = s.bindings[k]?.invoke().md
          
          markdown(
              "keys",
              """
              #### 1 — capture()
              ${captured.h}
          
              #### 2 — edited, then applied
              ${captured.diffHtml(edited, "captured", "edited")}
          
              #### 3 — the live structures, read back
          
              | binding | value |
              | --- | --- |
              | glow.radius | ${bound(glow, "radius")} |
              | glow.intensity | ${bound(glow, "intensity")} |
              | blur.radius | ${bound(blur, "radius")} |
              | glow.glow@radius | ${(glow.bindings["glow@radius"]?.invoke() ?: "<unbound>").md} |
          
              #### 4 — the bindings/values trap
          
              | binding | value |
              | --- | --- |
              | bound (via bind) | ${trap["bound"].md} |
              | set (via values) | ${trap["set"].md} {warn:← captured as null, silently} |
          
              #### 5 — captured() again, then re-captured
          
              ~~~
          ${captured.diffText(restored, "captured", "restored")}
              ~~~
          """,
              width = 800,
          )
  - create:
      box: keyframe_camera
      name: A camera move is a screw motion
      frame: { x: 80.0, y: 540.0, w: 320.0, h: 100.0 }
      properties:
        code: |
          /*
          KeyframeScope.camera stores a CameraPose — a rigid transform as a dual quaternion, plus
          the focus distance — rather than a position and a target point. Interpolating that is a
          SCREW MOTION, and between two cameras looking at the same subject it is a very different
          move from lerping the two positions. Draw both and the argument makes itself.
          */
          import afield.graphics.vulkan.util.CameraPose
          import afield.animation.keyframes.KeyframeScope
          import afield.math.linalg.Vector3f
          
          // The two camera positions; both look at the subject at the origin. Move one and rerun.
          var fromPos = Vector3f(8f, 2f, 0f)
          var toPos = Vector3f(0f, 2f, 8f)
          
          val scope = KeyframeScope()
          val a = scope.Key(mutableMapOf("camera" to CameraPose.lookAt(fromPos, Vector3f(0f, 0f, 0f))))
          val b = scope.Key(mutableMapOf("camera" to CameraPose.lookAt(toPos, Vector3f(0f, 0f, 0f))))
          val pa = (a["camera"] as CameraPose).position
          val pb = (b["camera"] as CameraPose).position
          
          val n = 60
          fun sclerpAt(t: Double) = (scope.interpolate(a, b, t)["camera"] as CameraPose)
          fun lerpAt(t: Double) = Vector3f(pa).lerp(pb, t.toFloat())
          
          // ---- panel 1: plan view, looking down y. World units scaled up to figure units.
          val S = 40.0
          val screw = fline {
              for (i in 0..n) {
                  val p = sclerpAt(i.toDouble() / n).position
                  if (i == 0) moveTo(p.x * S, p.z * S) else lineTo(p.x * S, p.z * S)
              }
              color = vec(0.36, 0.84, 1.0, 1.0)
              thickness = 3.0
          }
          val chord = fline {
              moveTo(pa.x * S, pa.z * S)
              lineTo(pb.x * S, pb.z * S)
              color = vec(1.0, 0.62, 0.26, 1.0)
              thickness = 3.0
          }
          // Sight lines from the sclerp path to the subject: every one is exactly the same length.
          val sight = fline {
              for (i in 0..10) {
                  val p = sclerpAt(i / 10.0).position
                  moveTo(p.x * S, p.z * S)
                  lineTo(0.0, 0.0)
              }
              color = vec(0.36, 0.84, 1.0, 0.22)
              thickness = 1.0
          }
          // …and from the lerped positions, which are visibly shorter through the middle.
          val sightLerp = fline {
              for (i in 0..10) {
                  val p = lerpAt(i / 10.0)
                  moveTo(p.x * S, p.z * S)
                  lineTo(0.0, 0.0)
              }
              color = vec(1.0, 0.62, 0.26, 0.22)
              thickness = 1.0
          }
          // The subject: a small circle at the origin.
          val subject = fline {
              circle(0, 0, 14)
              color = vec(0.95, 0.95, 0.95, 0.9)
              thickness = 2.0
          }
          
          // ---- panel 2: distance from the camera to the subject, against t.
          fun plotY(d: Double) = 330.0 - (d - 5.5) * 120.0
          val dScrew = fline {
              for (i in 0..n) {
                  val t = i.toDouble() / n
                  if (i == 0) moveTo(0.0, plotY(sclerpAt(t).position.length().toDouble()))
                  else lineTo(t * 400.0, plotY(sclerpAt(t).position.length().toDouble()))
              }
              color = vec(0.36, 0.84, 1.0, 1.0)
              thickness = 3.0
          }
          val dChord = fline {
              for (i in 0..n) {
                  val t = i.toDouble() / n
                  if (i == 0) moveTo(0.0, plotY(lerpAt(t).length().toDouble()))
                  else lineTo(t * 400.0, plotY(lerpAt(t).length().toDouble()))
              }
              color = vec(1.0, 0.62, 0.26, 1.0)
              thickness = 3.0
          }
          
          // Every number in the captions is measured here, never asserted from memory.
          val rMin = (0..n).minOf { sclerpAt(it.toDouble() / n).position.length() }
          val rMax = (0..n).maxOf { sclerpAt(it.toDouble() / n).position.length() }
          val worstAim = (0..n).maxOf { sclerpAt(it.toDouble() / n).target.length() }
          val lerpMid = lerpAt(0.5).length()
          val closer = (1.0 - lerpMid / rMax) * 100.0
          println("sclerp distance to subject: %.4f .. %.4f".format(rMin, rMax))
          println("straight-line midpoint:     %.4f  (%.1f%% nearer)".format(lerpMid, closer))
          println("worst-case aiming error:    %.6f world units".format(worstAim))
          
          showPlaneGrid(
              ("plan view, looking down y\n" +
                  "blue: sclerp, a quarter circle. orange: the straight line between the same two positions") to
                  listOf(sight, sightLerp, subject, chord, screw),
              ("distance to the subject, over the move\n" +
                  "sclerp holds %.4f..%.4f; the straight line dips to %.4f — %.1f%% nearer"
                      .format(
                          rMin,
                          rMax,
                          lerpMid,
                          closer,
                      )) to listOf(dScrew, dChord),
              columns = 2,
              cellWidth = 440,
              cellHeight = 380,
          )
          markdown(
              "aim",
              "worst-case aiming error along the sclerp path: **%.6f** world units — ".format(worstAim) +
                  "the subject never leaves the centre of frame.",
          )
  - create:
      box: keyframe_persist
      name: Saving is always additive history
      frame: { x: 1100.0, y: 80.0, w: 340.0, h: 100.0 }
      properties:
        code: |
          /*
          saveKey writes pretty JSON — and, every single time, ALSO appends a numbered copy to a
          <file>.versions directory with a manifest. Nothing prunes it, so a hundred saves leave a
          hundred files. What survives the trip is a closed set; everything else is dropped silently.
          */
          import afield.animation.keyframes.KeyframeScope
          import afield.math.linalg.Vector3f
          import afield.animation.keyframes.stackSLString
          import java.nio.file.Files
          
          val dir = Files.createTempDirectory("keyframer-demo")
          val path = dir.resolve("look.json")
          
          val scope = KeyframeScope(schemaVersion = 1)
          scope.saveKey(
              path,
              scope.Key(
                  mutableMapOf(
                      "gain" to 0.20f,
                      "pos" to Vector3f(1f, 2f, 3f),
                      "voice" to stackSLString("saw 110 *"),
                  ),
              ),
              note = "first pass",
          )
          
          scope.saveKey(
              path,
              scope.Key(
                  mutableMapOf(
                      "gain" to 0.65f,
                      "pos" to Vector3f(4f, 5f, 6f),
                      "voice" to stackSLString("sin 220 * fold"),
                  ),
              ),
              note = "brighter",
          )
          
          // A third save that also carries values the KValue union cannot represent.
          val lossy = scope.Key(
              mutableMapOf(
                  "gain" to 0.90f,
                  "enabled" to true, // a Boolean is outside the union
                  "taps" to listOf(1, 2, 3), // so is a list
                  "absent" to null, // and a null is dropped too
              ),
          )
          scope.saveKey(path, lossy, note = "with unsupported values")
          
          val versions = scope.keyVersions(path)
          versions.forEach { println("version ${it.index}  ${it.file}  ${it.note ?: "—"}") }
          
          val reloaded = scope.loadKey(path)
          val dropped = lossy.values.keys.sorted().filter { it !in reloaded.values.keys }
          println("third save kept: " + reloaded.values.keys.sorted())
          println("dropped in silence: " + dropped + "  <- no exception, no log line")
          
          // An older snapshot loaded into a scope that has since grown a parameter.
          val newer = KeyframeScope(schemaVersion = 1)
          newer.missingKey("wet", 0.5f) // applies to every file this scope loads
          newer.missingKey(1, "mode", "legacy-v1") // only to files stamped schemaVersion = 1
          val migrated = newer.loadKey(path, version = 0)
          println("version 0 migrated: " + migrated.values.toSortedMap())
          
          /*
          Rows built with joinToString and spliced into an indented block: markdown()'s dedent
          anchors on the first line, so the rows arriving at column 0 do not flatten the figure the
          way trimIndent would. The values table stays flat text rather than `migrated.h` — the
          Key's own HTML gives a Vector3f an interactive 3D axis widget, which reflows the card.
          */
          val versionRows =
              versions.joinToString("\n") { v ->
                  "| ${v.index} | ${v.file.md} | ${(v.note ?: "—").md} |"
              }
          val migratedRows =
              migrated.values.entries
                  .sortedBy { it.key }
                  .joinToString("\n") { (k, v) ->
                      "| ${k.md} | ${v.md} |"
                  }
          
          markdown(
              "persist",
              """
              #### version history after three saves
          
              | # | file | note |
              | --- | --- | --- |
              $versionRows
          
              #### third save: what survived
          
              kept: **${reloaded.values.keys.sorted().joinToString(", ")}**
          
              dropped in silence: {bad:${dropped.joinToString(", ")}}
          
              #### version 0, reloaded into a scope that has since grown a 'wet' parameter (${migrated.values.size} values)
          
              | key | value |
              | --- | --- |
              $migratedRows
          
              #### version 0 on disk, as written
          
              ~~~json
          ${Files.readString(dir.resolve("look.json.versions").resolve("000000.json"))}
              ~~~
          """,
              width = 820,
          )
  - create:
      box: keyframe_updatecode
      name: A captured look becomes source
      frame: { x: 1100.0, y: 640.0, w: 320.0, h: 100.0 }
      properties:
        code: |
          /*
          The last step of the loop closes it: Key.updateCode() emits the snapshot as pasteable
          Kotlin, so a state you arrived at by fiddling becomes a diff you can commit. Every
          literal is chosen so the paste round-trips as the same TYPE, not merely the same number.
          */
          import afield.animation.keyframes.KeyframeScope
          import afield.study.source.SourceBackedBlock
          import afield.math.linalg.Quaternionf
          import afield.math.linalg.Vector3f
          import afield.animation.keyframes.stackSLString
          
          val scope = KeyframeScope()
          val key = scope.Key(
              mutableMapOf(
                  "gain" to 0.65f, // a Float — and the 'f' suffix is load-bearing
                  "steps" to 12,
                  "seed" to 99L,
                  "pos" to Vector3f(1.5f, 0f, -2.25f),
                  "spin" to Quaternionf().setAngleAxis(0.7f, 0f, 1f, 0f),
                  "voice" to stackSLString("sin 220 * fold"),
                  /*
                  A source block whose body mentions a '$'. Emitted inside a Kotlin raw string it
                  would interpolate at paste time, so it must come out escaped.
                  */
                  "block" to SourceBackedBlock<Any?>("box-1", "val total = 2\nprintln(\"sum: \$total\")"),
                  "notes" to listOf("unsupported", "on purpose"),
              ),
          )
          
          val code = key.updateCode("look")
          println(code)
          
          // The round trip is about types: without the 'f', a captured Float pastes back a Double,
          // and Key.set deliberately does not re-coerce numbers.
          println("Float keeps its suffix: " + code.contains("0.65f"))
          println("Long keeps its suffix:  " + code.contains("99L"))
          // Check only the source-block line: the /* unsupported */ comment names the dropped Java
          // class, and a nested name like Arrays$ArrayList has a harmless '$' inside that comment.
          val blockLine = code.lines().first { it.contains("""this["block"]""") }
          println(
              "the source block's $ came out escaped: " + Regex("""(?<!\\)\$""").findAll(blockLine).none(),
          )
          
          display("code", "<pre>" + code + "</pre>")
  - execute:
      box: keyframe_targets
  - execute:
      box: keyframe_camera
  - execute:
      box: keyframe_persist
  - execute:
      box: keyframe_updatecode

          the focus distance — rather than a position and a target point. Interpolating that is a
          SCREW MOTION, and between two cameras looking at the same subject it is a very different
          move from lerping the two positions. Draw both and the argument makes itself.
          */

          var fromPos = Vector3f(8f, 2f, 0f)
          var toPos = Vector3f(0f, 2f, 8f)

          val a = scope.Key(mutableMapOf("camera" to CameraPose.lookAt(fromPos, Vector3f(0f, 0f, 0f))))
          val b = scope.Key(mutableMapOf("camera" to CameraPose.lookAt(toPos, Vector3f(0f, 0f, 0f))))
          val pa = (a["camera"] as CameraPose).position
          val pb = (b["camera"] as CameraPose).position

          val n = 60
          fun sclerpAt(t: Double) = (scope.interpolate(a, b, t)["camera"] as CameraPose)
          fun lerpAt(t: Double) = Vector3f(pa).lerp(pb, t.toFloat())

          // ---- panel 1: plan view, looking down y. World units scaled up to figure units.
          val S = 40.0
          val screw = fline {
              for (i in 0..n) {
                  val p = sclerpAt(i.toDouble() / n).position
                  if (i == 0) moveTo(p.x * S, p.z * S) else lineTo(p.x * S, p.z * S)
              }
              color = vec(0.36, 0.84, 1.0, 1.0)
              thickness = 3.0
          }
          val chord = fline {
              moveTo(pa.x * S, pa.z * S)
              lineTo(pb.x * S, pb.z * S)
              color = vec(1.0, 0.62, 0.26, 1.0)
              thickness = 3.0
          }
          // Sight lines from the sclerp path to the subject: every one is exactly the same length.
          val sight = fline {
              for (i in 0..10) {
                  val p = sclerpAt(i / 10.0).position
                  moveTo(p.x * S, p.z * S)
                  lineTo(0.0, 0.0)
              }
              color = vec(0.36, 0.84, 1.0, 0.22)
              thickness = 1.0
          }
          // …and from the lerped positions, which are visibly shorter through the middle.
          val sightLerp = fline {
              for (i in 0..10) {
                  val p = lerpAt(i / 10.0)
                  moveTo(p.x * S, p.z * S)
                  lineTo(0.0, 0.0)
              }
              color = vec(1.0, 0.62, 0.26, 0.22)
              thickness = 1.0
          }
          // The subject: a small circle at the origin.
          val subject = fline {
              circle(0, 0, 14)
              color = vec(0.95, 0.95, 0.95, 0.9)
              thickness = 2.0
          }

          // ---- panel 2: distance from the camera to the subject, against t.

          val dScrew = fline {
              for (i in 0..n) {

                  if (i == 0) moveTo(0.0, plotY(sclerpAt(t).position.length().toDouble()))
                  else lineTo(t * 400.0, plotY(sclerpAt(t).position.length().toDouble()))

                  else lineTo(t * 400.0, plotY(lerpAt(t).length().toDouble()))
              }

      properties:
        code: |
          /*
          saveKey writes pretty JSON — and, every single time, ALSO appends a numbered copy to a
          <file>.versions directory with a manifest. Nothing prunes it, so a hundred saves leave a
          hundred files. What survives the trip is a closed set; everything else is dropped silently.

                  "taps" to [1, 2, 3], // so is a list

          val reloaded = scope.loadKey(path)
          val dropped = lossy.values.keys.sorted().filter { it !in reloaded.values.keys }

          println("dropped in silence: " + dropped + "  <- no exception, no log line")

          val newer = KeyframeScope(schemaVersion = 1)
          newer.missingKey("wet", 0.5f) // applies to every file this scope loads
          newer.missingKey(1, "mode", "legacy-v1") // only to files stamped schemaVersion = 1

          println("version 0 migrated: " + migrated.values.toSortedMap())

          Rows built with joinToString and spliced into an indented block: markdown()'s dedent
          anchors on the first line, so the rows arriving at column 0 do not flatten the figure the
          way trimIndent would. The values table stays flat text rather than `migrated.h` — the
          Key's own HTML gives a Vector3f an interactive 3D axis widget, which reflows the card.

          val versionRows =

              }
          val migratedRows =
              migrated.values.entries
                  .sortedBy { it.key }
                  .joinToString("\n") { (k, v) ->
                      "| ${k.md} | ${v.md} |"
                  }

          markdown(
              "persist",
              """
              #### version history after three saves

              | # | file | note |
              | --- | --- | --- |
              $versionRows

              #### third save: what survived

              kept: **${reloaded.values.keys.sorted().joinToString(", ")}**

              dropped in silence: {bad:${dropped.joinToString(", ")}}

              #### version 0, reloaded into a scope that has since grown a 'wet' parameter (${migrated.values.size} values)

              | key | value |
              | --- | --- |
              $migratedRows

              #### version 0 on disk, as written

              ~~~json
          ${Files.readString(dir.resolve("look.json.versions").resolve("000000.json"))}
              ~~~
          """,
              width = 820,
          )
  - create:

      frame: { x: 1100.0, y: 640.0, w: 320.0, h: 100.0 }
      properties:
        code: |
          /*
          The last step of the loop closes it: Key.updateCode() emits the snapshot as pasteable
          Kotlin, so a state you arrived at by fiddling becomes a diff you can commit. Every
          literal is chosen so the paste round-trips as the same TYPE, not merely the same number.
          */
          val scope = KeyframeScope()
          val unsupportedNotes: List<String> = ["unsupported", "on purpose"]
          val key = scope.Key(
              mutableMapOf(
                  "gain" to 0.65f, // a Float — and the 'f' suffix is load-bearing
                  "steps" to 12,
                  "seed" to 99L,
                  "pos" to Vector3f(1.5f, 0f, -2.25f),
                  "spin" to Quaternionf().setAngleAxis(0.7f, 0f, 1f, 0f),
                  "voice" to stackSLString("sin 220 * fold"),
                  /*
                  A source block whose body mentions a '$'. Emitted inside a Kotlin raw string it
                  would interpolate at paste time, so it must come out escaped.
                  */
                  "block" to SourceBackedBlock<Any?>("box-1", "val total = 2\nprintln(\"sum: \$total\")"),
                  "notes" to unsupportedNotes,
              ),
          )

          val code = key.updateCode("look")
          println(code)

          // The round trip is about types: without the 'f', a captured Float pastes back a Double,
          // and Key.set deliberately does not re-coerce numbers.
          println("Float keeps its suffix: " + code.contains("0.65f"))
          println("Long keeps its suffix:  " + code.contains("99L"))
          // Check only the source-block line: the /* unsupported */ comment names the dropped Java
          // class, and a nested name like Arrays$ArrayList has a harmless '$' inside that comment.
          val blockLine = code.lines().first { it.contains("""this["block"]""") }
          println(
              "the source block's $ came out escaped: " + Regex("""(?<!\\)\$""").findAll(blockLine).none(),
          )

          display("code", "<pre>" + code + "</pre>")

  - execute:

          // operators d a k t g j n z o e s m b, with optional kN / tN degree indices. Re-run and
          // the whole contact sheet rebuilds — including the captions, which are read off the

          val expressions = listOf("C", "dC", "aC", "kC", "tC", "gC", "bC", "k4aC", "sD")

  renders it beside the identical plate without the ring, back-face culled, so the counterfactual is
  computed rather than described. Box 3 chains every named composite off one ambo — cube().ambo().bevel()

      box: polytope_face_with_a_hole

      properties:
        code: |

          // ***** CHANGE THIS LINE ***** the window's half-width, anywhere inside (0, 1).
          val solid = cubeWithWindow(side = 0.45f)

          val topology = solid.topology
          val windowed = topology.elements(2).single { topology.faceHasHoles(it.id) }
          val geometry = solid.triangulate()
          val rimTriangles = (0 until geometry.triangleCount).count { geometry.sourceFace(it) == windowed.id }

          // accidents: a Conway operator, a dualization and an OFF export are all defined for closed
          // manifolds, and a face with a hole is a surface with boundary.
          val refusals = listOf<Pair<String, () -> Any>>(
              "topology.dual()" to { topology.dual() },
              "solid.bevel()" to { solid.bevel() },
              "solid.toOff()" to { solid.toOff() },
              "triangulate(FanFaceTriangulator)" to { solid.triangulate(FanFaceTriangulator) },

              """

                  holes ${topology.faceHoles(windowed.id).map { it.size }}, rings ${topology.faceRings(windowed.id).size}

              triangles cut from the windowed face = $rimTriangles (a solid square would be 2)
              """.trimIndent(),

operations:

      box: youtube_vr_renderer
      name: window + renderer
      frame: { x: 40.0, y: 40.0, w: 320.0, h: 100.0 }
      properties:
        code: |
          import afield.graphics.vulkan.util.Options
          
          prop<Window>(window)
          prop<Renderer>(renderer)
          
          Options.enableHDR = false
          Options.profiling = false
          // OpenXR is the default on its supported desktop platforms. macOS remains the stereo
          // preview/development path because it has no system OpenXR runtime.
          Options.enableVR = !Options.isMac
          
          once.renderer {
              window = Window("YouTube · puppet browser")
              val created = Renderer(window)
              if (Options.enableVR) {
                  created.openXRHmdTarget = afield.graphics.vulkan.targets.OpenXRHmdTarget(created)
              }
              created
          }
          
          println("YouTube VR renderer ready")
          start(renderer::run)

      box: youtube_vr_panel
      name: YouTube — interactive Chromium panel
      frame: { x: 320.0, y: 140.0, w: 400.0, h: 100.0 }
      properties:
        code: |
          import afield.graphics.vulkan.Target
          import afield.media.browser.FieldUiBrowserTexture
          import afield.media.browser.PuppetBrowserVrPanel
          import afield.media.browser.PuppetBrowserWindowInput
          import afield.graphics.vulkan.targets.SideBySideStereoTarget
          
          // prop declarations are lifted into Field's preamble before ordinary imports are applied.
          prop<afield.media.browser.PuppetBrowser>(browserControl)
          
          // The producer is a full Chromium page, not an embed: consent, account state, player,
          // navigation and audio all behave as they do in an ordinary browser.
          val browser = FieldUiBrowserTexture(
              renderer = renderer,
              url = "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aqz-KE-bpKQ",
              width = 1280,
              height = 720,
              // Linux: Chromium's shared-texture export never fills the buffer (electron#53271).
              cpuBitmapFallback = FieldUiBrowserTexture.cpuBitmapFallbackRequired
          )
          browserControl = browser
